key_insight: Augmenting 2D reference images with estimated per-pixel depth turns an image-based representation into a geometry-aware, easy-to-update alternative to heavy 3D reconstructions, enabling accurate localization with image-to-image reasoning.
problem_solved: Closes the gap between lightweight 2D image-based localization (easy to build and maintain but geometrically limited) and accurate but cumbersome 3D structure-based methods (require centralized reconstruction and are hard to update).
method: Augment each reference image with estimated depth maps to encode local scene geometry (2.5D representation).
Use dense image-to-image matching that leverages both appearance and depth cues to establish robust correspondences for pose estimation.
Compute and verify camera poses using the image-based (depth-augmented) correspondences, avoiding a centralized 3D model and enabling easy dataset updates.
impact: Provides a practical localization pipeline that approaches 3D-method accuracy while keeping the simplicity and maintainability of image-based systems—useful for large-scale, dynamic, or resource-constrained deployment scenarios.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input image + predicted depth → dense matching → pose estimation

paper_title: ImLoc: Revisiting Visual Localization with Image-based Representation
paper_authors: Xudong Jiang, Fangjinhua Wang, Silvano Galliani, Christoph Vogel, Marc Pollefeys
